chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Walter Johnson, the smoothest drummer
summary: Walter Johnson never wilted a collar and still looked the same in his seventies.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Kaiser Marshall was the first one to have it. Then, of course, Walter Johnson.
Walter Johnson to me was the smoothest
drummer that I have ever heard.
And speaking of drummers, there was --
What was he like? Tell me --

A very quiet guy. Here was a guy that could play a gig all night long, play a four hour gig, it'd be hot in the place, and he would get through that night playing the drums and no wilted collar, no nothing. He looked just like he did when he came to work.
He always dressed impeccably, didn't he? Very --
Very neat, very neat, and the --

-- you know, and to this day if you see him -- he's an old man now and he still looks the same. He hasn't changed and he's in his seventies, and Walter Johnson looked just like he did back in the thirties.
